The Imaging Workflow From Order to Report, and Who Owns Each Step

Unit 1: Imaging Informatics Foundations. Lesson 1 of 65 in CIIP Academy.

A radiologist tells you a chest study is on the modality but missing from the reading worklist. Before you touch a server you need one thing: the map of every step between the clinician's order and the finished report, and which system owns each step. The exam thinks in workflows, not in boxes.

The steps, in order

Step                          Owner system            What can go wrong
1 Order entry                 EMR                     wrong procedure code, missing reason
2 Scheduling                  RIS or scheduling       appointment not sent to the RIS
3 Registration and ADT        registration system     demographics differ between systems
4 Modality worklist           RIS or broker           technologist types data by hand
5 Acquisition                 modality                wrong patient or laterality
6 Technologist QC             modality, PACS          image count short, study not sent
7 Storage                     PACS, archive           study not committed
8 Reading worklist            PACS or RIS             study never becomes read-ready
9 Reporting                   reporting system        report not matched to the order
10 Results distribution       interface engine, EMR   result lost in a queue
11 Billing                    billing system          charge not created

Who owns what

The EMR owns the order and the patient chart. The RIS owns scheduling and the radiology order status. PACS owns images and the reading worklist. The reporting system owns the report text and its status. The interface engine owns the movement of messages between them. When a step fails, you find the owner and the last system that saw the study.

Defining, implementing, and evaluating a solution

A workflow solution starts with a written description of the current steps and the problem, then a design that names the owner of each change, then a test with real studies, then go-live support, then measurement against the problem you started with.

Exam tip: trace the study step by step and ask which system last handled it. The FIRST action is almost always to identify the owner of the broken step, not to restart a server.
Remember
Eleven steps carry a study from order to bill, each owned by one system, and troubleshooting means finding the last system that saw the study.
Deeper explanation

The Imaging Workflow From Order to Report, and Who Owns Each Step, explained slowly

Following one study through the building

Take one real request: a clinician orders a two-view chest exam at 08:14 for an outpatient. The study will touch six systems before the bill is sent. If any step drops it, the symptom appears somewhere else, so the skill is tracing in order.

Time   Event                              System that holds the truth      Message or object
08:14  order placed                       EMR                              order message
08:15  order arrives, exam scheduled      RIS                              scheduling message
08:40  patient arrives, registered        registration                     patient message
08:52  technologist queries the worklist  RIS or broker                    worklist query
09:05  two images acquired                modality                         images, performed step
09:08  technologist checks count          PACS                             image count
09:10  study stored and committed         PACS                             storage commitment
09:12  study appears on reading list      PACS or RIS                      worklist entry
10:30  report signed                      reporting system                 result message
10:31  result shown in the chart          EMR                              result message

The trace method

When the radiologist says the study is missing, ask where it was last seen. If the images are on the modality but not in PACS, the break is between steps 5 and 7. If the images are in PACS but not on the list, the break is the study match to its order. If the report is signed but the clinician cannot see it, the break is the result message. Each case has a different owner and a different fix.

Worked example

The reading list is missing a chest study from 09:05. The technologist reports sending two images. PACS shows one image under the right patient. The count check from step 6 now tells you what happened: one image never arrived, so the study is incomplete and cannot become read-ready. The correct action is to have the technologist resend the missing image from the modality (which still holds it because storage commitment has not arrived), not to hold the radiologist waiting.

Defining, implementing, evaluating

Write the current workflow and its pain point first. Design the change by naming who owns each step. Test with real studies, including an unusual one such as a stat case. After go-live, measure the same time points you measured before and compare. If you cannot show the before and after, the change is not evaluated.
